Berkshire reported approximately 20.7 million shares of Bending Spoons valued at about $689 million as of Q3 end.

Bank of America remained a major holding but was reduced by about 5.7%, or roughly 27.5 million shares.

Apple continued as the firm's largest position at about 228 million shares, representing roughly 25% of the equity portfolio and valued near $76 billion as of September end.

Berkshire Hathaway opened a new position in Bending Spoons (BSP) and sharply increased its stake in Lennar during the third quarter, while also adding to Delta Air Lines and Macy's while trimming several existing holdings, including Bank of America, Verisign, and Capital One.

According to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday, the firm's overall equity portfolio stood at roughly $304 billion across about 30 positions as of the end of the quarter.

New And Expanded Positions

Berkshire reported approximately 20.7 million shares of Bending Spoons valued at about $689 million as of Q3 end. Lennar saw the largest stake increase among existing names, with Class A shares nearly doubling to around 26 million and the position reaching roughly $2.1 billion. The company also added to its Lennar Class B shares.

Delta Air Lines holdings rose by about 12% to 64.5 million shares, worth approximately $5.4 billion. Berkshire slightly increased its Macy's holding in the third quarter, raising the position by about 2.6% to roughly 7.5 million shares.

LEN and BSP stocks each gained 1% after-hours on the filing. DAL and M shares traded flat.

Trims And Reductions

Bank of America remained a major holding but was reduced by about 5.7%, or roughly 27.5 million shares, bringing the position to approximately 456 million shares valued near $24.8 billion.

Verisign holdings were cut by roughly one-third, Capital One by more than 60%, and Kroger by about 10%. Smaller reductions occurred in Nucor and DaVita. No positions were fully exited during the quarter.

VRSN shares slipped 2% after hours while BAC stock traded marginally in the red, as did NUE and DVA.

Largest Holdings Unchanged

Apple continued as the firm's largest position at about 228 million shares, representing roughly 25% of the equity portfolio and valued near $76 billion as of September end. American Express, Coca-Cola, and Alphabet remained among the top holdings with no reported share changes. Chevron, Occidental Petroleum, Moody's, Chubb, Kraft Heinz, Sirius XM, Ally Financial, and the New York Times also showed no share adjustments.

The moves offer an early glimpse into how Chief Executive Greg Abel is steering the $1 trillion conglomerate's investment portfolio following his succession of Warren Buffett in January, with Berkshire continuing to adjust its holdings across financial services, technology, consumer and industrial companies.

Berkshire reduced its Bank of America stake by 6% to 455.9 million shares, valued at approximately $24.8 billion at the end of September. Its investment in Capital One fell sharply, declining 62% to 1.15 million shares worth about $222 million. By contrast, Berkshire increased its Delta Air Lines position by 12% to 64.5 million shares, valued at $5.38 billion.

The filing, which details Berkshire's U.S.-listed equity holdings as of September 30, covers the bulk of its $335.5 billion stock portfolio. Berkshire purchased $2.37 billion in equities during the quarter and sold $2.79 billion, continuing its recent trend of being a net seller of stocks.

Berkshire has traditionally favoured concentrated investments in businesses with durable competitive advantages, strong cash generation and established market positions. Its latest portfolio changes come as investors watch whether Abel will maintain the disciplined, long-term approach that defined Buffett's investment strategy or gradually introduce a different allocation of capital.

Berkshire also disclosed a new investment in Bending Spoons, an Italian technology company that owns Vimeo and AOL. The investment included $600 million committed to the company's initial public offering in July and a further $330 million invested in October, taking its position to roughly 4%.

In another notable move, Berkshire approximately doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar during the third quarter. Following additional purchases in October, its ownership had climbed to 12.5% of the company.

Berkshire Hathaway sold Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) again in the third quarter. The company's new 13F filing, released Monday afternoon, shows 455,860,908 shares on September 30, down from 483,394,015 on June 30.

The numbers

Berkshire sold 27,533,107 shares in the quarter, 5.7% of its stake. At Bank of America's September 30 price of $54.43, those shares were worth about $1.50 billion. It was the largest sale by dollar value in the filing.

Alex Wong / Getty Images News via Getty Images

It was the second straight quarter of selling. Berkshire held 513,624,165 shares on March 31, so 57,763,257 shares, or 11.2%, have been sold in six months. Berkshire held more than 1 billion Bank of America shares in mid-2024, so more than half of that stake is gone.

What is left

Bank of America is still the fifth-largest stock in the filing. The remaining shares were worth $24.81 billion on September 30, 8.2% of the $304.20 billion of stocks Berkshire lists.

Bank of America closed at $50.11 on Monday, 7.9% below its September 30 price. At that price the remaining stake is worth about $22.84 billion.

Berkshire also cut another bank stock in the quarter. Its Capital One holding fell from 3,000,000 shares to 1,150,000.

title: Chase Confirms Banking Glitch As Thousands Report Outages. Bank Of America, Wells Fargo Also Flagged.
detail:
Chase Confirms Banking Glitch As Thousands Report Outages. Bank Of America, Wells Fargo Also Flagged.
Merin Rebecca Thomas
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 2:25 PM CST 3 min read
BAC
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
A Chase Bank branch in Chicago, Illinois, on April 13, 2026. Getty Images

JPMorgan Chase confirmed a technical problem affecting some banking transactions Monday as thousands of customers reported trouble accessing financial services at several major U.S. banks, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank.

The complaints, recorded by outage-tracking website Downdetector, involved difficulties logging into online banking accounts, using mobile apps and completing transactions.

Chase acknowledged that some transactions were taking longer than usual but said customers could still access their accounts and funds.

"Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds," a Chase spokesperson told The Associated Press.

The bank said it was working to resolve the problem and described the disruption as a technical issue rather than a cyberattack.

Some Chase customers encountered notices stating that certain services were temporarily unavailable and asking them to try again later.

According to Barron's, customer complaints began climbing shortly after 9 a.m. Eastern Time.

Downdetector recorded 4,822 reports involving Chase shortly before 2 p.m. ET, along with more than 2,000 reports for Bank of America and more than 1,000 for U.S. Bank.

The tracking website also recorded 968 complaints involving Wells Fargo, 188 for PNC Bank and 103 for Citigroup, according to Barron's.

Those figures reflect customer-submitted reports at particular times, not the number of customers confirmed to have been affected by technical failures.

The reports involving multiple institutions raised questions about whether the disruptions were connected, although the statements from banks did not establish a common technical failure.

U.S. Bank told the Associated Press that its own systems were not directly affected.

However, the bank said customers sending or receiving money through Zelle with another financial institution could experience transaction delays.

Zelle is a payment network operated by Early Warning Services, which is owned by several major banks, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and others.

A spokesperson for Zelle told NBC Chicago that the reported payment disruption was a Chase issue.

That distinction is important because delays involving transfers between banks do not necessarily indicate separate outages at every institution receiving customer complaints.

ABC7 News also reported Chase's confirmation of the technical issue in its live coverage Monday.

title: Canadian inflation holds at 3.1% in October as core measures remain near target
detail:
Canadian inflation holds at 3.1% in October as core measures remain near target
Proactive
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM CST 1 min read
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Canadian inflation holds at 3.1% in October as core measures remain near target Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Canadian inflation held steady at 3.1% in October, while underlying price pressures remained relatively subdued, strengthening the case for the Bank of Canada to hold interest rates steady at its next meeting.

The Consumer Price Index rose 3.1% year over year, unchanged from September and below the 3.2% increase expected by economists, according to Bank of America analysis.

On a monthly basis, headline inflation increased 0.2%, compared with 0.1% in September and below the 0.3% forecast.

Higher gasoline prices continued to put upward pressure on the headline figure, rising 30.9% year over year compared with 27.8% in September. Excluding gasoline, inflation was unchanged at 2.2%.

The average of the Bank of Canada's preferred core inflation measures held at 1.9% in October, with core median unchanged at 2% and core trim easing to 1.8%, as goods inflation accelerated to 4.3% while services inflation slowed to 2.1%.

Bank of America now expects headline inflation to reach 2.9% by the end of 2026, slightly higher than its previous forecast of 2.8%, before returning to 2% by the end of 2027.

Energy prices remain the main upside risk, particularly given uncertainty surrounding the conflict involving Iran. On the downside, the bank warned that trade uncertainty could undermine Canada's economic recovery.

For interest rates, Bank of America expects the Bank of Canada to deliver another 25-basis-point increase but sees January as the more likely timing rather than December.

Although inflation remains above target and the central bank has left the door open to further tightening, Bank of America said domestic economic conditions argue for patience.

How many reports

Downdetector's figures are reports from users. They are a count of complaints, and the banks have not said how many customers are affected.

What customers are seeing

Some customers reported trouble with their bank's app. Others said they could not cash checks, withdraw or transfer money, or process cashier's checks, Newsweek reported.
